newsitem.title: ITALY: NATO general urges arrest of war crimes suspects.
newsitem.headline: NATO general urges arrest of war crimes suspects.

text.p: NATO's supreme commander in Europe, General Wesley Clark, on Tuesday urged leaders in the former Yugoslavia to arrest indicted war criminals and hand them over to the United Nations for trial.

"In Bosnia we have to push on with the process of political reconciliation and, for that to be possible, we need to fulfil the Dayton peace accord," he told a news conference in this southern Italian city, home of NATO's southern command.
"(Yugoslav President Slobodan) Milosevic and the other Bosnian Serb leaders have agreed to work with the Hague international war crimes tribunal by signing the accord," he said.
"Primary responsibility for handing over war criminals rests with them."

The arrest of indicted war criminals has proved one of the biggest obstacles preventing the full implementation of the U.S.-brokered Dayton accord, signed by the presidents of Serbia, Bosnia and Croatia in December 1995 to end the Balkan war.
The NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR), which replaced the NATO-led Implementation Force, has refused to round up suspects who continue to work in positions of power.
The two most prominent suspects, former Bosnian Serb President Radovan Karadzic and his former military commander Ratko Mladic, remain at large.
The U.N. tribunal in The Hague has no police force of its own and relies on the former Yugoslav republics, other states or international troops in Bosnia to make arrests.
Clark declined to speculate on Bosnia's future after June 1998, when SFOR's mandate ends.
"I'm not looking at next June," he said. "I'm looking at tomorrow, I'm looking at next week. There's still a lot to do."
